claims.text: High-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings resist time-dependent plastic deformation better than composition- and thickness-matched monolithic coatings.
The relevant multilayer coatings contain coherent, chemically distinct interlayer interfaces.
Engineered interlayer interfaces impede dislocation motion.
Engineered interlayer interfaces especially impede dislocation climb and dynamic recovery.
Impeded dislocation motion delays creep deformation relative to a monolithic coating.
Multilayer and monolithic coatings can be compared while holding overall composition and thickness constant.
Dislocation climb and dynamic recovery govern time-dependent deformation under the proposed elevated thermal and mechanical loading conditions.
Coherent and chemically distinct interlayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Multilayer interfaces block and pin dislocations.
Multilayer interfaces reduce the ability of dislocations to climb and rearrange during sustained loading.
Multilayer interfaces increase the effective activation energy for dislocation motion relative to a monolithic structure.
Multilayer coatings will accumulate significantly less creep strain than matched monolithic coatings.
Multilayer coatings will have higher yield strength than matched monolithic coatings under the proposed tests.
Multilayer coatings will have higher creep activation energy than matched monolithic coatings.
The proposed mechanism should dominate only where dislocation climb and dynamic recovery are the primary rate-limiting deformation mechanisms.
Creep deformation can instead be controlled by lattice diffusion of alloy constituents.
At very high temperatures or when diffusion or alternative deformation modes become significant, the interfacial barrier effect may diminish.
The exact magnitude and statistical significance of the creep-resistance improvement across service conditions remain unquantified.
Failure to observe significantly reduced creep strain or evidence of interfacial dislocation pinning would falsify the proposed interfacial mechanism.
